Y = list(Y1, Y2, Y3, Y4, Y5) Yi vector trait - Ni individuals. colocboost also offers flexible input options (see detailed usage different input formats, refer Individual Data Colocalization.): Single X matrix N * P Y matrix N * L L traits. title: Input Data Format
text: analyses using summary statistics, basic format single trait follows: sumstat data frame required columns z (beta, sebeta), optional columns highly recommended n variant. LD matrix LD. matrix need contain exact variants sumstat, colnames rownames LD include variant names proper alignment. input format multiple traits similar, sumstat list data frames sumstat = list(sumstat1, sumstat2, sumstat3). flexibility input format multiple traits follows (see detailed usage different input formats, refer Summary Statistics Colocalization.):: One LD matrix superset variants sumstat traits allowed. title: Interpret ColocBoost Output
text: dataset features two causal variants indices 644 2289. Causal variant 644 associated traits 1, 2, 3, 4. Causal variant 2289 associated traits 2, 3, 5. cos_summary object contains colocalization summary colocalization events, row representing single colocalization event. summary includes following columns: focal_outcome: focal outcome analyzed, FALSE focal outcome exists. colocalized_outcomes: Traits colocalized within 95% colocalization confidence set (CoS). cos_id: unique identifier 95% colocalization confidence set (CoS). purity: minimum absolute correlation variants within 95% colocalization confidence set (CoS). top_variable: variable highest variant colocalization probability (VCP). top_variable_vcp: variant colocalization probability top variable. cos_npc: normalized probability colocalization 95% confidence set, providing empirical evidence favor colocalization trait-specific configuration. min_npc_outcome: minimum normalized probability among colocalized traits. n_variables: number variables 95% colocalization confidence set (CoS). colocalized_index: indices colocalized variables. colocalized_variables: list colocalized variables. colocalized_variables_vcp: variant colocalization probabilities colocalized variables. obtain summary colocalization specific focus traits interest, can use get_cos_summary, see detailed usage function link. function allows filter colocalization summary based particular outcome interest, making easier interpret results specific traits. example, interested colocalization events involving traits Y1 Y2, can use following code:
code: # Loading the Dataset data(Ind_5traits) # Run colocboost  res <- colocboost(X = Ind_5traits$X, Y = Ind_5traits$Y) #> Starting checking the input data. #> Starting gradient boosting algorithm. #> Boosting iterations for outcome 4 converge after 34 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 5 converge after 43 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 1 converge after 46 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 2 converge after 67 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 3 converge after 68 iterations! #> Starting assemble analyses and results summary. cos_summary <- res$cos_summary names(cos_summary) #>  [1] "focal_outcome"             "colocalized_outcomes"      #>  [3] "cos_id"                    "purity"                    #>  [5] "top_variable"              "top_variable_vcp"          #>  [7] "cos_npc"                   "min_npc_outcome"           #>  [9] "n_variables"               "colocalized_index"         #> [11] "colocalized_variables"     "colocalized_variables_vcp" # Get summary table of colocalization cos_interest_outcome <- get_cos_summary(res, interest_outcome = c("Y1", "Y2"))

title: Interpret ColocBoost Output
text: cos_summary, 95% CoS, cos_npc column provides normalized probability colocalization min_npc_outcome column provides minimum normalized probability among colocalized traits. two metrices measured empirical evidence colocalization CoS-level trait-level. obtain best minimal colocalization configuration can defined using cos_npc npc_outcome See detailed usage function link. output get_strong_colocalization output colocboost, can directly used post inference visualization.
code: filter_res <- get_strong_colocalization(res, cos_npc_cutoff = 0.5, npc_outcome_cutoff = 0.2) #> Extracting colocalization results with cos_npc_cutoff = 0.5 and npc_outcome_cutoff = 0.2. #> For each CoS, keep the outcomes configurations that the npc_outcome > 0.2.

title: Visualization of ColocBoost Results
text: default plot colocboost results provides visual representation colocalization events. x-axis indicates indices variants y-axis indicates -log10(p-value) marginal associations. colors points represent colocalization events, different colors indicating different colocalization events.  Parameters adjust plot plot_cols = 2 (default) indicates number columns plot. y = "z_original" z-scores y = "vcp" variant colocalization probabilities, y = "coef" regression coefficients estimated colocboost model. plot_cos_idx = NULL (default) indicates colocalization events plotted. plot_cos_idx = 1 can specified plot 1st colocalization event, . outcome_idx = NULL (default) indicates traits colocalization plotted. outcome_idx = c(1,2,5) can specified plot traits 1, 2, 5. cos_color = NULL (default) indicates colors colocalization events. Specify vector colors customize plot.
code: colocboost_plot(res)

what: ColocBoost: A gradient boosting informed multi-omics xQTL colocalization method — colocboost
title: ColocBoost: A gradient boosting informed multi-omics xQTL colocalization method — colocboost
text: colocboost implements proximity adaptive smoothing gradient boosting approach multi-trait colocalization gene loci, accommodating multiple causal variants. method, introduced Cao et al. title: ColocBoost: A gradient boosting informed multi-omics xQTL colocalization method — colocboost
code: # colocboost example set.seed(1) N = 1000 P = 100 # Generate X with LD structure sigma <- 0.9^abs(outer(1:P, 1:P, "-")) X <- MASS::mvrnorm(N, rep(0, P), sigma) colnames(X) <- paste0("SNP", 1:P) L = 3 true_beta <- matrix(0, P, L) true_beta[10, 1] <- 0.5  # SNP10 affects trait 1 true_beta[10, 2] <- 0.4  # SNP10 also affects trait 2 (colocalized) true_beta[50, 2] <- 0.3 # SNP50 only affects trait 2 true_beta[80, 3] <- 0.6 # SNP80 only affects trait 3 Y <- matrix(0, N, L) for (l in 1:L){  Y[, l] <- X %*% true_beta[, l] + rnorm(N, 0, 1) } res <- colocboost(X = X, Y = Y) #> Starting checking the input data. #> Starting gradient boosting algorithm. #> Boosting iterations for outcome 1 converge after 98 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 3 converge after 106 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 2 converge after 107 iterations! #> Starting assemble analyses and results summary. res$cos_details$cos$cos_index #> $`cos1:y1_y2` #> [1] 10  9 #>
